seen_animation: A line-drawn baseball bat (wide barrel at left, narrow handle at right with three tape marks and a hooked knob) is held by two drawn arms, each a pair of parallel lines ending in a rounded loop hand. Grey scenery of a house, a mushroom-shaped tree and a round tree sits on a horizon line at the top and does not move. In frames 1-4 the bat is tilted up toward the right, sitting in the middle of the frame. In frames 5-9 it lowers, rotates to horizontal and slides left while getting longer. In frames 10-16 it keeps rotating until the handle end points down to the lower right, the barrel end reaches the left edge, and the right arm straightens to vertical. The last frames hold this pose.
seen_film: A boy in a patterned short-sleeve shirt stands in a schoolyard holding a baseball bat across his waist with both hands, while girls play in the background. In frames 1-4 he looks down and the bat is tilted up to the right. In frames 5-9 he lowers the bat to horizontal and it extends further to the right, and he begins to look to his right. In frames 10-16 the bat is held lower across his thighs, the barrel to the left and the handle tilted down to the lower right, while he looks over his shoulder and then down again. The bat holds nearly still in the last third.
named_subject: A baseball bat held by two drawn arms/hands (the doodle is the bat alone).
evidence: Orientation matches the film at the same moments: e.png 1-8 the bat tilts up-right as in f.png 1-8; e.png 9-14 it passes through horizontal as in f.png 9-14; e.png 15-26 it tilts down-right and settles, as in f.png 15-26 where the bat lies low with the handle end dropping right. Placement matches: in e.png 26 the bat spans from near the left edge to near the right edge in the lower part of the frame, as in f.png 26. g.png shows an even fan of positions rotating clockwise and drifting left with no gaps or reversals. Consecutive frames in e.png change by small, steady amounts with no pops, doubling or size jumps; the growth in length from e.png 1 to 16 is gradual and matches the film's bat turning from pointing into depth to lying across the frame. Film frame f.png 2 is a motion-blurred frame with a slight camera shift; the animation does not reproduce it, which is acceptable. Judged from still frames only, not playback.
primary_gap: The two arms with loop hands are added strokes that do not exist in the reference doodle, so part of the black-line character is not the c.png drawing.
closes_when: The arms either disappear (bat alone moving as in the doodle) or are reduced to minimal hand marks drawn with the same single-weight line and blunt corners as the doodle, while the bat stays identical.
protect: The bat's construction copied from c.png (blunt flat barrel end, tapering outline, three tape ticks, hooked knob); the clockwise rotation timed to the film (up-right in 1-8, level by 9-14, down-right by 15-26); the leftward drift and gradual lengthening; the still hold at the end; the stable grey scenery; the absence of any pops between frames.
identity_gap: The bat is clearly the c.png drawing, but the arms and loop hands are invented additions in a doubled-line style not present in the doodle.
